title: Telemetry-first SDK handshake and tool safety PRD
content:
Executive summary:

This PRD proposes a telemetry-first handshake and tool-safety surface for the Hosted API SDKs. The goal is to make tool-calling and structured streaming observable by default, reduce integration friction for customers, and provide deterministic signals for performance and quality regressions. Unlike prior drafts that focused primarily on framing partial responses and low-level frames, this proposal puts telemetry and safety signals into the handshake itself so instruments can be attached from session-start and persisted through rollouts and fallbacks.

Why now:
- Customers increasingly embed complex tool graphs (external APIs, internal microservices, DB lookups) which complicate troubleshooting when multi-hop requests degrade.
- Observability blind spots make it slow to triage regressions that surface as subtle latency spikes or tool-call misroutings.
- We need deterministic telemetry tied to model variants, client SDK versions, and per-request tool metadata to enable Optimize suggestions and automated regression alerts.

Top-level objectives (SMART):
- Instrument 90% of SDK-hosted tool-call flows with token-level telemetry by end of Q1 2025 (measured by instrumented sessions sampled in telemetry pipeline).
- Reduce mean time to root cause (MTTR) for tool-related incidents by 50% within three months after rollout, measured by internal incident reviews.
- Provide a stable, small-surface handshake that SDKs can implement in <= 100 lines of integration code for most languages.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not redesign streaming frame wire formats; it layers a minimal handshake and telemetry envelope on top of existing streaming protocols.
- Not addressing authorization model changes (KMS/HSM) — assume existing token/KV patterns.
- Not trying to entirely eliminate client-side parsing complexity for rich tool outputs — aim to make it easier, not perfect for all edge cases.

User personas and primary flows:
- Platform engineer: wants end-to-end traces showing model -> tool -> backend durations and easy correlation to route, model version, and SDK version.
- Product engineer embedding a Hosted API chat: needs clear failure modes for tool calls (abort, fallback, degrade) and actionable logs.
- SRE / Oncall: needs deterministic telemetry to configure alerts on tool call error-rate regressions and token-cost anomalies.

Core design principles:
- Telemetry-by-default: handshake must enable structured telemetry without opt-in heavy config.
- Minimal footprint: handshake should add few extra RTTs and small metadata payloads.
- Backward compatible: clients without new fields should continue to work; server should degrade gracefully.
- Privacy-aware: telemetry must not include PII; include scrubber guidance and allow sampling.
- SDK ergonomics-first: default client APIs should favor simple streaming callbacks/promises with small opt-in knobs for advanced telemetry.

Handshake overview (session-start):
1) CLIENT -> SERVER: session_start (client_sdk: {name, version}, preferred_telemetry_level, session_id_hint, declared_tools)
   - declared_tools: compact list of tool metadata the client intends to call in this session (name, id, optional capabilities tag). Not required but recommended for richer traces.
2) SERVER -> CLIENT: session_ack (server_version, active_model, telemetry_token, telemetry_sampling_rate, supported_tool_contracts)
   - telemetry_token: short-lived opaque id to correlate telemetry events for this session. Tied to sample decision.

Why a telemetry_token?
- It allows high-cardinality correlation without leaking user tokens. It’s rotated per session and can be used by internal collectors to join traces across services (model server, dedicated routing, tool proxies).

Telemetry levels: none | minimal | verbose
- none: only high-level request/response markers (default for low-cost endpoints).
- minimal: per-request durations, tool call start/end, HTTP status codes (no token accounting).
- verbose: token-level counters, prefix/KV cache hits, per-tool token delta, sketch of output size and structured field counts.

Event model (emitted by SDK and server):
- session.start, session.ack, request.start, token.batch.emitted, tool.call.start, tool.call.end, tool.call.error, response.partial, response.complete, cache.hit, fallback.trigger, session.end
- Each event carries TTL-safe metadata: session_id (telemetry_token), model_id, route, sdk_name/version, tool_id (if applicable), timestamp, duration_ms, feature_flags

Telemetry payload constraints:
- Events must be small (<= 2KB typical) and avoid free-text user content. For structured outputs we include only shape metadata (fields present, array lengths) and a checksum/simhash for content-level correlation.

Tool-calling semantics and safety surface:
- Tool declarations (optional) let the platform validate tool contracts ahead of calls and surface mismatches.
- Tools must return a structured tool_response wrapper when available: {status, code, shape_signature, safe_preview}
  - safe_preview: optional sanitized excerpt (<= 512 chars) used only for telemetry when verbose level is enabled.
- Tool safety modes:
  - strict: any tool error aborts the response and returns tool.failure to client.
  - degrade: tool failure returns a best-effort synthesized fallback and marks fallback.trigger telemetry.
  - observer: tool results are advisory only (used for scoring), errors are silent in the primary response but logged.

Structured output typing and evolution:
- The server returns a structured schema id with each complete response when structured output was requested. Schema ids map to versioned JSON-schema-like descriptors in the model catalog.
- Clients MAY cache schema descriptors locally and validate partial/complete responses against the schema for early UX hints.
- To support backward-compatibility, schema changes are additive by default. Breaking changes must be versioned and surfaced via the handshake supported_tool_contracts/docs link.

Streaming and partial response guidance:
- Partial frames include frame_type and optional shape_annotations. Frame types: narrative_chunk, tool_frame, schema_patch, checkpoint.
- SDKs should expose two simple primitives:
  - onPartial(frame): called for partial frames with shape annotations; emit telemetry.response.partial with frame metadata.
  - onCommit(schema_id, final_payload_summary): final commit; SDK emits telemetry.response.complete and optionally triggers client-side validation.
- Backpressure: handshake includes a preferred_batch_ms hint. SDKs should allow host apps to override batching via sendOptions to balance latency and cost.

SDK ergonomics (recommended high-level API patterns):
- StreamingPromise pattern (JS/TS): createSession(...).stream({onPartial, onTool, onComplete, onError}) returns a disposable handle. This reduces cognitive load compared to raw event parsers.
- Typed helper: client.generateTyped(schemaId, prompt) -> returns a typed object on completion and raises a ValidationError if schema mismatch detected.
- Tools adapter: tools are registered locally with a compact descriptor that maps name->callable. SDKs handle marshalling and emit tool.call.start/end telemetry automatically when using the adapter. Developers should be able to opt out and call tool endpoints manually for advanced flows.

Observability and storage considerations:
- Sampling: default telemetry sampling_rate is 1% for verbose, 10% for minimal. Customers can configure through Console per-organization.
- Storage retention: high-cardinality event traces retained 30 days; aggregated rollups retained 365 days for Optimize integration.
- Cost signals: telemetry includes per-session token delta estimates (server-side computed) and per-tool approximate token delta (where available). These enable Optimize to recommend quantization or batch window changes.

Migration and compatibility story:
- Servers accept legacy session_start without preferred_telemetry_level and default to minimal for known customers, none for anonymous beta routes.
- SDKs implement a compatibility mode that will not emit session.start if the server uses a legacy ack format; the client logs a compatibility warning in debug telemetry only.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Alpha (internal): SDKs for Node/Python + server feature flag. Collect initial telemetry and iterate on event schema (2 weeks).
- Beta (selected customers): opt-in via Console and SDK flag. Monitor MTTR and telemetry event volumes. (6 weeks).
- GA: enabled-by-default for new routes; existing routes may opt into minimal by Console toggle. (Q2 2025 target).

Success metrics (examples):
- Coverage: percent of sessions with session.start + session.end events >= 90% within 30 days of GA.
- MTTR: median incidence triage time for tool-call incidents reduced by 50% vs baseline.
- Telemetry volume efficiency: 95th percentile event size < 1.5KB and data egress growth < 6% of current traffic.
- SRE alert precision: false-positive rate of tool-error alerts < 10% due to improved telemetry.

Security and privacy:
- Telemetry_token must be opaque and not reversible to customer tokens. Internal mapping stored in a short-lived cache with strict RBAC.
- Telemetry scrubber guidance enforced: SDKs include a sanitizer library that replaces emails, SSNs, and URLs in any safe_preview field. Customers can supply custom scrubbers via configuration.

Open questions and tradeoffs:
- How much semantic information should safe_preview contain? More helps debugging but risks PII leakage. Proposed compromise: 512-char sanitized preview, removed by default for strict privacy tiers.
- Cost of verbose token-level telemetry at scale — will need dynamic sampling and an adaptive sampling controller backed by the platform.
- Will tool contracts become a vendor-managed schema registry? If yes, we need lifecycle APIs for pushing and deprecating contracts.

Appendix: short examples
- JS streaming usage (sketch):
  const s = client.createSession({declared_tools: [{id: 'search',capabilities:['query']}], preferred_telemetry_level: 'minimal'});
  const handle = await s.stream({
    onPartial(frame){ console.log('partial', frame.meta); },
    onTool(toolFrame){ console.log('tool', toolFrame); },
    onComplete(res){ console.log('done', res); }
  });

- Example telemetry event (flattened for pipeline):
  event: "tool.call.end", session: "tkn_3f9a", sdk: "js-0.18.2", model: "redwood-chat-v1", tool: "search", duration_ms: "120", status: "200", token_delta_est: "42"

Next steps and owners:
- Product (Jordan): finalize event schema and telemetry levels; prepare Console toggles (2 weeks).
- Applied ML (Luca, Mei): define model-side token-delta calculation and schema_id contract flow (3 weeks).
- SDK (Priya, Samir): implement Node and Python prototypes and attach scrubber library (4 weeks).
- Observability (Evelyn): wire events into trace pipeline and create initial dashboards/alerts (3 weeks).

FAQ (anticipated):
Q: Will remaining SDKs (mobile, java, go) follow?
A: Yes — Node/Python are prototypes. Mobile/Go/Java follow in the Beta after feedback.

Q: Does this change billing?
A: No billing changes, but telemetry enables better internal cost attribution and Optimize recommendations.

Q: Can customers disable telemetry entirely?
A: Console-level toggles available. Defaults may vary by tier.

Document history:
- 2024-11-12: initial draft
- 2024-12-05: added tool safety modes and sampling guidance
- 2025-01-20: refined handshake and telemetry_token lifecycle
- 2025-02-02: updated rollout plan and owners

End of PRD draft.
